title: Improve clinical dengue outcomes with an approved direct-acting antiviral

concept.text: Treat early dengue infection with an antiviral that reduces clinically important illness or progression. Mosnodenvir demonstrated human prophylactic antiviral activity, but that does not establish therapeutic benefit; its phase 2 field-prevention programme was discontinued. Proposed completion test: Regulatory approval following a randomized phase 3 trial in naturally infected patients treated early in illness, showing superiority on a prespecified clinical endpoint such as progression to severe dengue, hospitalization or sustained symptom resolution, with virological outcomes supportive. Test set by: A regulator would decide approval; no universally accepted dengue-antiviral efficacy threshold was identified. The clinical endpoint and early-treatment requirement are proposed editorial criteria. Overlaps: VIR-02. Sources given: [Primary mosnodenvir prophylaxis trial record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41297006/?fc=None&ff=20260215191432&v=2.18.0.post22+67771e2) ; [Sponsor announcement discontinuing the field-prevention study](https://www.jnj.com/media-center/press-releases/johnson-johnson-to-discontinue-phase-2-field-study-evaluating-investigational-antiviral-for-the-prevention-of-dengue).

page.title: Approved direct-acting antiviral treatment for dengue
page.definition: An approved medicine that targets dengue virus and reduces clinical illness in infected patients. Direct-acting antivirals inhibit a viral component; they include small molecules and virus-neutralizing monoclonal antibodies.

goal.need: WHO received 7,718,585 laboratory-confirmed dengue case reports in 2024. CDC’s guidance dated 15 April 2026 states that there is no specific antiviral treatment. Treatment development addresses illness in people already infected.

figures.caption: Global dengue reports received by WHO for 2024
figures.note: Surveillance counts, not estimates of all infections.

statements.quote: pan-serotype efficacy in reducing symptom duration and preferably also progression to severe dengue.
statements.context: Desired efficacy of treatments for non-severe dengue; pan-serotype means activity against all four dengue serotypes.

statements.body: Drugs for Neglected Diseases initiative, SII dengue mAb programme
statements.quote: Develop a safe, effective, and globally accessible therapeutic for dengue

completion.title: FDA approves a direct-acting antiviral with a clinical treatment benefit in dengue.
completion.criterion: FDA grants marketing approval through a new drug application for a small molecule or a biologics licence application for an antibody, with an indication for treating symptomatic dengue. The approved prescribing information establishes the clinical treatment benefit and the population in which benefits outweigh risks. The applicable approval requirements for effectiveness, safety, product quality and labeling are satisfied.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration; approval standards described in Benefit-Risk Assessment for New Drug and Biological Products, section II.A.
completion.threshold_quote: must determine that the drug is safe and effective for use under the conditions prescribed, recommended, or suggested in the product’s labeling.
completion.basis: Marketing approval supplies an externally adjudicated test of the treatment claim and its benefit–risk balance. FDA describes this determination as specific to the proposed indication and population. WHO’s treatment profile seeks shorter clinical illness and preferably less progression to severe dengue; an antiviral laboratory signal alone does not establish those benefits.

milestones.title: Preclinical evidence supports initial human dosing of a dengue antiviral.
milestones.criterion: Pharmacology and toxicology findings support initial human exposure. Small molecules: the JNJ-1802 clinical report describes preceding activity against all four dengue serotypes in cells and mice. Antibodies: the VIS513 first-in-human report states that human testing followed confirmation of preclinical safety and efficacy. These publications establish progression from laboratory development into human testing.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Development and Review Definitions, Pre-Clinical Research; a general drug-development criterion.
milestones.threshold_quote: the drug is reasonably safe for use in initial, small-scale clinical studies.

milestones.title: A dengue antiviral has human safety and exposure data sufficient for phase 2 dose selection.
milestones.criterion: Human safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetic findings support controlled phase 2 studies. JNJ-1802, reported on 10 May 2023, had 39 single-dose and 47 multiple-dose participants; two drug-related grade 2 rashes resolved, and terminal half-life was 6.3–9.2 days. VIS513, reported on 23 February 2024, had 40 adults: 34 antibody and 6 placebo recipients. No serious adverse events occurred; 28 antibody recipients had treatment-related adverse events.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Development and Review Definitions, Phase I Clinical Studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: to permit the design of well-controlled, scientifically valid, Phase 2 studies.

milestones.title: A regulator authorizes a randomized dengue-antiviral treatment trial in infected patients.
milestones.criterion: A medicines regulator permits a randomized, placebo-controlled treatment trial in confirmed dengue. Anvisa announced authorization of EYU688 phase 2a on 22 October 2024; the sponsor listed recruiting status on 10 November 2026, with 108 participants planned. The Indian regulator approved the Dengue-mAb phase 2 protocol; 250 adults were randomized at 12 Indian hospitals from 19 September 2021 to 13 May 2023.
milestones.set_by: Anvisa, EYU688 phase 2a authorization notice; this notice concerns a small molecule. Indian regulatory authorization of the antibody protocol is documented in the Dengue-mAb trial report.
milestones.threshold_quote: Aprovação refere-se ao ensaio clínico Fase 2a de medicamento de uso oral, inibidor de replicação dos quatro sorotipos do vírus da dengue.

milestones.title: A dengue antiviral lowers infectious virus in blood at 24 hours versus placebo with P<0.05.
milestones.criterion: Treatment starts within 48 hours of fever onset and improves the prespecified 24-hour infectious-virus endpoint at two-sided P<0.05. Dengue-mAb’s single-blind study randomized 250 adults; 249 were dosed and 32 had baseline infectious viraemia. At 7 mg/kg, the difference in log10 viral reduction was 1.02 (95% CI 0.41–1.63; P=0.001; 7 versus 8 evaluable). DENV-4 was absent. AT-752’s 21-person trial had a nonevaluable primary endpoint. Mosnodenvir showed prophylactic activity in 10 high-dose versus 7 placebo recipients, P<0.001; field prevention was discontinued on 4 October 2024 in a sponsor announcement, not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: Serum Institute of India, Dengue-mAb-02 phase 2 protocol and published statistical analysis. The 24-hour endpoint and significance criterion were published for an antibody.
milestones.threshold_quote: Two-tailed P < .05 was considered statistically significant.

milestones.title: A dengue antiviral shortens sustained recovery versus placebo in a phase 3 treatment trial.
milestones.criterion: A randomized, double-blind phase 3 trial demonstrates shorter time to sustained recovery versus placebo, with supportive care in both groups. DNDi’s registered antibody protocol includes patients aged ≥5 years with antigen- or PCR-confirmed dengue, without warning signs or severe dengue, treated within 72 hours of symptom onset. Recovery assessments include temperature, haematocrit, platelets and absence of warning signs or severe dengue, assessed daily from day 1 to day 28. The registry contains no efficacy results.
milestones.set_by: Drugs for Neglected Diseases initiative, protocol DNDi-DmAb-01-DEN, ISRCTN50970152. This published clinical endpoint is specified for a monoclonal antibody.
milestones.threshold_quote: Demonstrate that Dengue monoclonal antibody compared to placebo reduces the time to sustained recovery from dengue fever

not_found: No dengue-specific FDA or EMA numerical minimum clinical effect size was found.
ISRCTN50970152 does not publish sustained-recovery cutoffs, a target sample size or a statistical success boundary.
No published phase 3 dengue-treatment efficacy result was found for either modality.
The WHO-hosted treatment-profile PDF was inaccessible; an archived copy of the WHO document was accessible.
Publisher full texts of the VIS513 phase 1 and AT-752 phase 2 papers were inaccessible; their indexed PubMed abstracts were available.

results.finding: JNJ-1802 showed activity against all 4 dengue serotypes in vitro and in mice; preclinical sample size not reported.
results.detail: The first-in-human study included 86 healthy participants. The report describes preceding preclinical activity and subsequent human dosing.
results.quote: In addition, in vitro and mice experiments have shown that this compound has potent activity against all 4 serotypes, which are genetically diverse [ 9 ].

results.finding: VIS513: 40 healthy adults received antibody or placebo in the first-in-human study after preclinical safety and efficacy were confirmed.
results.quote: After confirmation of safety and efficacy in preclinical studies, it was tested in a first-in-human study to assess the safety and pharmacokinetics.

results.finding: JNJ-1802: 39 single-dose and 47 multiple-dose participants; terminal half-life was 6.3–9.2 days.
results.detail: JNJ-1802 was generally safe and well-tolerated. Two drug-related grade 2 rashes resolved. The phase 1 safety and pharmacokinetic results helped guide dose selection for future trials.
results.quote: The results from this FIH study together with the preclinical results [ 9 ] were used to guide dose selection for future clinical trials with JNJ-1802.

results.finding: VIS513: 40 adults participated; 28 of 34 antibody recipients had treatment-related adverse events.
results.detail: No serious adverse events occurred. Median elimination half-life ranged from 775 to 878 hours; the authors reported dose-proportionate exposure and supported further evaluation in dengue patients.
results.quote: Of these 143 adverse events, 80 were treatment-related adverse events in 28 (82%) of 34 participants.

results.finding: Anvisa authorized a phase 2a trial of an oral dengue antiviral on 22 October 2024; sample size not stated.
results.detail: The announcement does not state whether the trial is randomized or placebo-controlled, or whether participants have confirmed dengue.
results.quote: Aprovação refere-se ao ensaio clínico Fase 2a de medicamento de uso oral, inibidor de replicação dos quatro sorotipos do vírus da dengue.

results.finding: India’s regulator approved the Dengue-mAb trial protocol; 250 adults were randomized.
results.detail: The phase 2 treatment trial was randomized, single-blind and placebo-controlled. Eligibility required a positive rapid dengue NS1 antigen test.

results.finding: Dengue-mAb 7 mg/kg (7 evaluable vs 8 placebo): 24-hour infectious viral log reduction difference 1.02; P=0.001.
results.detail: The primary endpoint used an infectious-virus assay. Fever onset was based on participant recall; the authors noted that some participants may have been treated later than 48 hours after onset. DENV-4 was not detected.
